This Wp Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of
The Constitution Of India, 1950 Praying To A) Quash
The General Award Passed By The R3 Bearing No.
Kiadb/Laq/2019-2023-24 Dated 06/06/2023 In Respect Of
Sy. No. 97/P5, Jmc Block No. 16 Measuring To An Extent
Of 2 Acres 30 Guntas Situated At Doddagollahalli
Village, Kundana Hobali, Devanahalli Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District As Per Annexure-A And Etc.,
 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Additional Government Advocate is directed to take notice for respondent No.1 and Sri P. V.
Chandrashekar, learned counsel is directed to notice for respondent Nos.2 and 3.
NC: 2023:KHC:37175 2.

This petition is filed seeking to set aside the general award dated 06.06.2023 passed by the third respondent in respect of land bearing survey No.97/P5, JMC Block No.16 measuring 2 acres 30 guntas situated at Doddagollahalli village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District as per Annexure-1 and for further direction to the respondent Nos.2 and 3 to consider the case of the petitioner under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966 for determination of compensation by way of an agreement.

3. The case of the petitioner is that, he is the owner of aforesaid land which has been acquired by the respondent KIAD in terms of the notification dated 25.05.2022 under Section 28(1) of the KIAD Act,
1966; that though the petitioner has no objection in respondent authorities acquiring the land, the respondent authorities have proceeded to pass the general award.

He submits that, as regards subsequent acquisition, suit in O.S.No.719/2023 had been filed and the said suit has now been Sri. Doddaanjinappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87498077/
2 compromised by a compromise decree dated NC: 2023:KHC:37175 02.09.2023 in terms of which the subject property has been allotted to the petitioner.

entities.text: Sri. Doddaanjinappa vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that now there is no impediment of any nature whatsoever in respondent authorities determining the compensation under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966.
4. In response Sri. P. V. Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing for respondent-KIADB submits that the general award was passed in view of the pendency of the suit.

Now that the petitioner is contending a compromise decree has been arrived at, on verification of the same, the requisition of the petitioner for consideration of his case under Section 29(2) would be done.
5. Accepting the above submission, petition is allowed, general award dated 06.06.2023 is set aside to the extent of the land belonging to the petitioner herein above.
(i) The petitioner shall make a  representation along with the requisite documents enabling the respondent authorities to consider his case under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966.

NC: 2023:KHC:37175 (ii) The respondent authorities are at liberty to call for further records if required and after satisfying itself shall pass the award within a period of three months in terms of Section 29(2) of the Act 1966.
(iii) If there is any dispute with regard to title the general award passed shall stand restored.
Deposit made if any before the Court by respondent authorities are at liberty to withdraw the deposit made if any.
